title: What if you fell through a tunnel in Earth? #shorts
description:
Explore the physics of a theoretical gravity train. Learn how gravity would accelerate you toward the center and decelerate you on the other side.

Sources (Wikipedia, CC BY-SA):
- Gravity train: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity_train
- Gravity: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity

scenes.say: What if you fell through a straight tunnel through the Earth?
You would accelerate toward the center using nothing but gravity.
During the first half of the trip, the downward pull increases your speed.
As you approach the core, gravity pulls you harder.
Once you pass the center, the direction of the pull flips.
Your momentum from the first half carries you upward through the second half.
This deceleration acts like a brake, slowing you down as you climb.
In a perfect vacuum, your speed would reach zero exactly as you reach the other side.
You would end up exactly where you started, without ever using fuel.
A journey powered entirely by the planet's own mass.
